texts.preamble: Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P. on 30 April, 2019 Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench Court No. - 28 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 118 of 2004 Revisionist :- Ram Adhar Opposite Party :- The State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Saurabh Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J. 1.
texts.facts: 2. The facts of the case are that the Food Inspector Sri Upendra singh intercepted the revisionist, who was taking 110 litres of milk in six cans on a Rickshaw for selling the same. After introducing himself, he bought 750 ml milk for Rs.5.25/- and after preparing sample, sent it to public analyst for examination. No one from the public came to be witness regarding sample etc. The revisionist Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P. on 30 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47403219/ 1 refused to reveal the name of the owner of the milk. The public analyst in his report found the milk solids-not-fat much below of 18%, which is prescribed under the Act for the milk. Since the milk sent for analysis was found to be adulterated one, a compliant was filed. The complaint was filed on 15.10.1992 and the notice was issued under Section 13(2) of the Act on 30.10.1992.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the sample was taken on 29.7.1991 and analysis report was dated 3.9.1991. He, therefore, submits that the notice was not served within a period of six months and the samples become unfit for analysis after ten months and, therefore, the sample along with the analysis report could not be sent to the Central Food Laboratory for further analysis. He further submits that since there is violation of Section 13(2) of the Act, the whole proceedings got vitiated and the judgments and orders passed by the courts below are liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. In support of his submission, learned counsel for the revisionist has placed reliance upon the judgement of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in the case of Suresh Narayan and others v. State of M.P., 2003 FAJ 322. Paragraph six of the aforesaid judgement reads as under :- "6. The Supreme Court in both the above mentioned cases have considered this aspect and in the case of State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid (supra) recorded its concurrence with the exercise of power under section 482 by the Punjab & Harayana High Court, quashing the proceedings pending against accused persons before the trial Court because the prosecution was filed after the lapse of long time and accused deprived of valuable right to get sample reanalised from Central Insecticide Laboratory which has prejudiced the case of the accused. Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, the proceedings pending before the learned CJM, Indore in Case No. 5247/95 is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]." 7. On the other hand, Sri Ashwani Kumar Singh, learned AGA submits that the revisionist gave wrong address and, therefore, notice could not be served and for his own wrong, he cannot be given the benefit. 10. Considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, in which the Supreme Court after considering the age of the appellant in that case and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone. 11.
